definition: A midbrain hub of the auditory pathway, between the brainstem auditory nuclei and the medial geniculate body of the thalamus.
Computer systems that perform tasks that normally need human intelligence, such as recognising images or understanding language.
The visual area next to V1, which it surrounds. It takes V1's output and responds to somewhat more complex features, such as illusory contours and border ownership.
The change in a neuron's membrane potential caused by input at a synapse: excitatory (EPSP) if it depolarizes, inhibitory (IPSP) if it hyperpolarizes.
When a system's state depends on its history, e.g. a neuron that starts firing at one current but stops at a lower one.
The set of functions and rules a library or service offers to programs that use it.
A hardware description language for designing digital circuits such as FPGA designs (Verilog is the other common one).
A class of layer 5/6 pyramidal cell whose axon stays mostly near home, with few long-range targets; a smaller group beside IT, ET and CT cells.
A free, open-source mixed-signal circuit simulator descended from Berkeley SPICE3, with XSPICE code models, CIDER device simulation and Verilog-A models loaded through OSDI.
A text description of a circuit: one line per element naming its nodes and value or model, plus dot commands for models, parameters and analyses.
The way SPICE builds its circuit equations: Kirchhoff's current law at every node, plus one extra equation and unknown (a branch current) for each voltage source and inductor.
The method SPICE uses to solve nonlinear circuit equations: linearise every device at the present guess, solve the linear system, and repeat until the changes are below the tolerances.
The part of an ngspice netlist between .control and .endc, a script in ngspice's own language that runs analyses, computes with result vectors, measures and writes files.
Running ngspice with -b: it carries out the netlist's dot analyses and output lines without waiting for input; a .control block should then end with quit or contain the analyses itself.
The SPICE3 result file holding all saved vectors of a run, binary by default or text with set filetype=ascii; written with -r or the write command.
ngspice's user start-up script, read after spinit and before the netlist, from the netlist's folder, the current folder or home; used to set compatibility modes, options and osdi loads.
The ngspice variable ngbehavior, whose flags (ps, lt, hs, spe, ki, a ...) make ngspice accept PSpice, LTspice, HSPICE, Spectre or KiCad syntax in model files or the whole netlist.
A letter after a number in a netlist: T, G, Meg, k, m, u, n, p, f, a and mil. M and m both mean milli; mega is Meg.
Writing component values with the multiplier as the decimal point, as on resistor markings: 2K7 for 2.7 kilohms, 4R7 for 4.7 ohms; accepted by ngspice in LTspice mode.
An ngspice element whose voltage or current is an arbitrary expression of node voltages, branch currents, time and temperature, evaluated at every iteration.
A compiled C model loaded into ngspice from a .cm library and used through an A element: analog blocks like gain, limit and s_xfer, digital gates, and bridges between them.
The XSPICE code model for a Laplace transfer function, given as numerator and denominator coefficients in s; ngspice's replacement for the LAPLACE option of other simulators.
A source whose value depends on another voltage or current: E (voltage-controlled voltage), G (voltage-controlled current), F (current-controlled current) and H (current-controlled voltage).
A source waveform given as time-value pairs joined by straight lines; in ngspice r= repeats it and td= delays it.
Random noise added to a transient run by TRNOISE sources: white Gaussian, 1/f and random telegraph noise sampled at a set interval, for noise in circuits whose operating point moves.
A voltage source marked with portnum and z0 for S-parameter analysis; it gets a series resistance z0 that stays in every analysis.
Splitting a transistor model into parameter sets valid for ranges of L and W (lmin, lmax, wmin, wmax), named nch.1, nch.2 ...; the simulator picks the bin that contains each device's size.
The standard SPICE bipolar transistor model (ngspice BJT level 1), with high-injection, Early effect, charge storage and series resistances.
An extension of the Gummel-Poon bipolar model with a parasitic substrate transistor, quasi-saturation and self-heating; ngspice BJT level 4.
A physics-based compact model for SiGe heterojunction bipolar transistors from TU Dresden; ngspice has HICUM/L2 built in (level 8) and other versions via Verilog-A.
ngspice's power-MOSFET model, compatible with LTspice's VDMOS model cards, with weak inversion, quasi-saturation, self-heating and a body diode.
ngspice's netlist front end that evaluates .param lines and expressions in braces once, when the netlist is expanded, before the simulation starts.
A netlist function giving a nominal value plus a Gaussian random deviation: agauss(nom, avar, sigma) has standard deviation avar/sigma; gauss() takes a relative deviation.
A reusable block of a netlist defined between .subckt and .ends with its own nodes and parameters, and placed with an X line.
The name of an element or node inside a subcircuit as seen from the top, such as v(x1.n3) or @m.x1.m2[gm] in ngspice.
A named part of a SPICE library file between .lib name and .endl, included with .lib file name; PDKs use one section per process corner.
A foundry's package of device models, corner libraries, layout rules and cells for a manufacturing process; open ones include SkyWater SKY130, GF180MCU and IHP SG13G2.
IHP's open 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS process; its MOSFETs use the PSP 103 model in Verilog-A, loaded into ngspice through OSDI.
SkyWater's open 130 nm CMOS process and PDK, with BSIM4 models in ngspice format; device sizes are given in microns because its library sets .option scale=1e-6.
GlobalFoundries' open 180 nm CMOS process and PDK for 3.3 V and 6 V designs, with ngspice models in sm141064.ngspice.
The DC solution of a circuit with capacitors open and inductors shorted; small-signal analyses linearise around it and transients start from it.
A DC convergence aid: put a large conductance across every junction, solve, and reduce it step by step, each solution starting the next.
A DC convergence aid that ramps all independent sources from zero to their full values, solving at each step.
A netlist command giving starting guesses for node voltages in the operating-point iteration; the solution may move away from them.
A way to simulate the exact loop gain of a feedback circuit from two AC runs, one injecting a series voltage and one a shunt current at the same point, without breaking the DC path.
Minus the derivative of phase with respect to angular frequency; the delay a narrow-band signal's envelope sees through a system.
The error an integration formula makes in one time step; SPICE estimates it from capacitor charges and inductor fluxes to choose the next step.
SPICE's default integration formula for transient analysis: second order with no numerical damping, so it preserves oscillations but can show trap ringing.
Backward-differentiation integration formulas of order 2 to 6; they damp numerical ringing and handle stiff circuits but also damp real oscillations slightly.
A numerical artefact of trapezoidal integration: after an abrupt change, a quantity such as an inductor voltage flips sign at every time step.
A time at which the simulator must place a time point, such as a corner of a PULSE or PWL source; the step is reduced after it.
A weighting applied to a time record before an FFT to reduce leakage between bins: Hanning, Blackman, flat-top and others trade resolution against sidelobe level and amplitude accuracy.
An analysis that finds the poles and zeros of a linearised circuit's transfer function, in radians per second.
An analysis that computes the derivative of an output with respect to every component value and model parameter at the operating point (or over frequency).
The ratios of reflected and transmitted to incident waves at the ports of a network for a reference impedance (usually 50 ohms); S11 is input reflection, S21 forward transmission.
The standard text file format for S-parameter data (.s1p, .s2p ...); ngspice writes two-port files with wrs2p.
The periodic solution a driven or oscillating circuit settles into; the shooting method finds it by iterating on the state at the start of one period instead of simulating the whole start-up.
An array of real or complex results in ngspice, such as v(out) or time, held in a plot and manipulated with let in the control language.
A named set of vectors produced by one analysis run (op1, ac1, tran1 ...); setplot switches between them.
The ngspice command that changes a .param value; it takes effect after reset re-expands the netlist.
The SPICE statement and ngspice command that extract numbers from results: delays, crossings, averages, rms, integrals and expressions.
The ngspice command that writes vectors as plain columns of numbers for gnuplot, spreadsheets or numpy.
An ngspice 47 command that plots vectors with Python's matplotlib, optionally straight to a PNG file.
A control-language loop that reloads a circuit once per process corner (and often per voltage and temperature), since ngspice has no .step.
The ngspice command that fixes the random-number seed so Monte Carlo and noise runs are repeatable.
A simulator error meaning the circuit equations have no unique solution, usually a node without a DC path to ground or a loop of voltage sources and inductors.
The transient error raised when no solution is found even at the minimum time step; usually caused by discontinuities, missing capacitance or poor tolerances.
An ngspice command that finds the operating point by a short pseudo-transient with ramped sources, for circuits whose ordinary DC solution fails.
A simulator-independent interface for compiled device models; ngspice loads .osdi shared libraries made by OpenVAF from Verilog-A.
A Verilog-A compiler that turns compact device models into .osdi shared libraries; continued as OpenVAF-Reloaded.
The analog subset of Verilog-AMS, used to publish compact device models as equations for branch currents and voltages.
The ngspice control command that loads an .osdi model library before the circuit is parsed.
A Verilog-A exponential whose growth is limited during Newton iterations, so device models do not overflow while the simulator searches for a solution.
An XSPICE node that changes only at discrete times and carries a digital state (0, 1 or U with a strength) or other event data.
XSPICE code models that convert between analog voltages and digital event nodes, with thresholds or output levels.
The XSPICE code model that runs compiled Verilog (Verilator, Icarus) or VHDL (GHDL) as a digital block in an ngspice circuit.
ngspice built as a shared library that another program loads and drives through a C API, as KiCad does.
ngspice's coupled circuit and 1D/2D semiconductor device simulator, which models diodes, BJTs and MOSFETs from doping and mesh instead of compact models.
A disturbance caused by one ionising particle striking a circuit; ngspice's seegen code model injects the resulting current pulses.
